verdict: Adobe posted record revenue of $6.6B, up 13%, with AI-first recurring revenue tripling past $500M — but a goodwill impairment charge held GAAP profit growth to just 1%, at $1.7B.

kpis.label: Total ARR
kpis.note: annualized recurring revenue, incl. ~$480M from Semrush

segments.name: Subscription
segments.note: Creative Cloud, Acrobat and Experience Cloud subscriptions — 97 cents of every revenue dollar. Creative & Marketing Professionals paid $4,540M (+13%); Business Professionals & Consumers paid $1,850M (+16%).

segments.name: Product
segments.note: One-time software licenses — a small legacy line from before Adobe moved to subscriptions.

segments.name: Services and other
segments.note: Consulting, training and support services sold alongside the software.

flow.costPlain: Running Adobe's cloud services — data centers, customer support and the cost of delivering its software.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building Photoshop, Acrobat, Firefly AI and the rest of the product line.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Sales teams, advertising and marketing — Adobe's biggest running cost.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day: finance, legal, HR, offices — this quarter it also carries a goodwill impairment charge (see one-time items).

opex.name: Amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of technology and customer relationships bought in past acquisitions.

otherDetail: Non-operating items netted to exactly zero: $65M of interest expense was offset by $18M of investment gains and $47M of other income.

takeaways.title: AI-first products are a real business now
takeaways.text: Recurring revenue from Adobe's AI-first products tripled year over year and passed $500M, and total ARR ended the quarter at $27.10B — including about $480M from the newly acquired Semrush.

takeaways.title: The subscription machine
takeaways.text: Subscriptions were $6,416M of the $6,618M total, and remaining performance obligations (contracted future revenue) reached $22.27B. Very little of Adobe's revenue has to be re-won each quarter.

takeaways.title: Profit barely grew
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 13% but net income only 1%, to $1,712M. A goodwill impairment charge and heavy spending weighed on GAAP profit; non-GAAP net income, which sets those aside, was $2.40B. Adobe still raised its full-year revenue and non-GAAP EPS targets.

oneTimers: GAAP results include a non-cash goodwill impairment charge of $0.17 per share related to the Publishing & Advertising reporting unit — it is the main reason GAAP EPS ($4.25) trails the non-GAAP figure ($5.96) by more than stock pay alone would explain.
Adobe closed its Semrush acquisition during the period: Semrush added roughly $480M of ARR and about $40M of subscription revenue in the quarter, and Adobe's updated full-year targets include it.
Adobe also announced a CFO change with this print: Dan Durn departed on June 15, 2026, with Steve Day, a 20-year Adobe finance leader, serving as interim CFO.
